subject: Post-demo recap: Searchly model-fit, prompt samples, and next steps
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aaron Feldman <aaron@searchly.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: Searchly model-fit, prompt samples, and next steps

Hi Aaron —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we have a clean handoff to technical evaluation: 

What we covered (TL;DR)
- Core goal: extract structured metadata and redact PII from user-uploaded documents at ingestion, then generate short search snippets for UI.
- Priority use-cases: (1) PII redaction, (2) consistent snippet quality across long docs, (3) cost-sensitive inference for high throughput.

Immediate asks / next steps from Searchly
1) Share a small sample set of real prompts and the problematic edge cases you see in the wild (examples of where current models hallucinate or fail to redact). We discussed a CSV with columns: prompt_text, expected_output, should_redact (yes/no), notes.
2) Any internal redaction policy or examples (we can map to our redaction guidance).
3) Confirmation on SLA/latency targets and throughput expectations so we can size Dedicated or Hosted options.

What we'll deliver
- Ben will follow up with recommended model candidates and an initial benchmark plan (latency/cost/quality trade-offs).
- We'll run a quick 1k-prompt sweep once we receive your CSV and return a short report with redaction precision/recall and regression flags.

Attachments: I also attached a short template (stub) for the prompt CSV to make it easy to export.

Proposed schedule
- Please send samples by EOD Wednesday (Oct 7).
- We’ll run the sweep and share preliminary results by Oct 12.

Let me know if any of the asks above need adjusting. Thanks again — excited to help on this.

—
Grace O'Connor
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-2147

Attachments: prompt_csv_template.csv (CSV stub)

Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 17:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Searchly model-fit, prompt samples, and next steps

Thanks Grace — great demo. Attaching a first-pass CSV and our internal redaction doc. A few notes inline below.

Attached: searchly_prompt_samples.csv, searchly_redaction_guidance.docx

Quick context on the CSV (2 short examples included inline):
- row 1: prompt_text = "Extract customer name and last purchase date from invoice text" | expected_output = "{\"customer_name\":\"Acme Corp\", \"last_purchase\":\"2026-09-18\"}" | should_redact = no
- row 2 (edge case): prompt_text = "Summarize user message and remove any emails or SSNs" | expected_output = "short summary without emails/SSNs" | should_redact = yes (contains emails)

Redaction policy summary: we need automated redaction for emails, phone numbers, SSNs, and account numbers. Prefer redaction-first approach (mask PII) before generating snippets to avoid leakage.

Questions for you:
- Can Redwood's suggested models do redaction deterministically (preferably token-level mask outputs) or will we need a separate entity-extraction+post-process?
- For cost, we care about per-request token cost at 256–512 token contexts; current traffic estimate ~800 rps peak.

We should be available for a short sync tomorrow morning if you want to walk through the CSV.

Best,
Aaron
Director of Product, Searchly
aaron@searchly.ai

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Searchly model-fit, prompt samples, and next steps

Aaron —

Received, thanks for the CSV and redaction doc. I skimmed the two rows and the structure looks good. A couple of small asks to make our sweep more actionable: 

1) Edge-case labeling: for rows where should_redact = yes, can you add a column fail_mode with values like "partial_masking", "over_redact", "missed_entity"? That helps our automated evaluation classify failure modes.
2) Expected output format: if you can include an expected_output_normalized column with a normalized JSON string (consistent keys), that makes metric calculation deterministic.
3) Privacy: redaction-first workflow is preferred. We can run an entity-extraction model (high-precision tagger) + deterministic token mask step before any generative snippet. If you want token-level masks returned, let us know the mask token you prefer (e.g., [REDACTED]).

Benchmarks and evaluation plan (what Ben will run)
- Quality: redaction precision/recall, snippet faithfulness (ROUGE/QA against ground truth), hallucination rate over the sample set.
- Cost/Perf: median p50/p95 latency at your target concurrency, tokens/request, and estimated $/1M tokens.
- Regression checks: we’ll run a basic A/B vs a reference model and flag regressions on your priority prompt subset.

If you’re comfortable with that scope, Ben will schedule the sweep and return a short report. Can you confirm you’re ok with token masking as the default redaction output? Also confirm whether any of the CSV rows are considered highly sensitive (we can handle via Private deployment if needed).

Proposed quick sync: Wed Oct 7 at 9:00am PT — Ben, Marissa and I can join.

—
Grace O'Connor
Solution Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: Searchly model-fit, prompt samples, and next steps

Aaron / Grace — looping in a short recommendation based on Searchly's priority (redaction + snippet quality + throughput).

Model candidates (initial):
- rw-infer-13b-high-ctx (recommended for best snippet quality on long docs; higher token cost but lower hallucination)
- rw-infer-3b-enc-slim (good middle ground for extraction/redaction tasks; much lower cost, faster p95)
- redwood-llama2-13b-q4 (quantized option if you want lower cost with modest quality tradeoff)

Evaluation plan (what we'll run once CSV updated):
- Run entity-extraction baseline (deterministic tagger) to produce token masks.
- Generate snippets from both masked and unmasked flows to compare leakage/hallucination.
- Compute: redaction precision/recall, snippet F1 vs expected_output_normalized, hallucination rate (unreferenced facts), p50/p95 latency and estimated token cost.

Benchmarks / helpful links:
- Internal sweep runner: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C_searchly_eval_materials (we'll put results here)
- Public perf guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.com/perf/throughput-latency

Operational questions for sizing:
- Confirm whether you expect bursts above 800 rps (if yes, we should talk Dedicated burst pools).
- Confirm retention requirements for prompt logs (default 30 days on Hosted).

Plan: once you update the CSV with fail_mode and expected_output_normalized we’ll kick off a 1k prompt sweep across the three models and share a short report within 3 business days. If there are highly sensitive rows, flag them and we can run that subset in Private.

Happy to run the Wed 9am PT sync.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
